book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 36 · Toxicology: Substance Abuse and Poisoning
title: Gases, Pesticides, Medicines and Bites: What the PCP Can Do

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already give high-flow oxygen, decontaminate skin and give IM epinephrine for anaphylaxis. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Treat toxic gases: CO, cyanide, chlorine, and the BC protocols that apply
  2. Recognize pesticide, household and medication poisonings, and what's outside BC scope
  3. Manage bites and stings, and see where your IV, fluids and D10W fit

Textbook: Chapter 36, PDF pages 3127–3197 (Carbon Monoxide to Bites and Stings)
slides.say: Welcome to the last part of toxicology. As EMRs, you already know to get patients out of a toxic environment, give high-flow oxygen, decontaminate the skin, and give IM epinephrine for anaphylaxis. Today we cover the poisons that don't come from the street. First, toxic gases: carbon monoxide, cyanide and chlorine, and the BC protocols you'll use for them. Second, pesticides, household chemicals and overdoses of medicines like acetaminophen and antidepressants. The textbook lists many antidotes here, and most are outside BC scope, so you need to know what you can actually do. Third, bites and stings. Throughout, watch where the PCP's IV, fluids and D10W come in.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到毒理学的最后一部分。作为 EMR，你们已经知道要把病人移出有毒环境、给高流量氧、给皮肤洗消，以及对过敏性休克肌注肾上腺素。今天讲不是来自街头毒品的毒物。第一，有毒气体：一氧化碳、氰化物和氯气，以及对应的 BC 流程。第二，农药、家用化学品，以及对乙酰氨基酚、抗抑郁药等药物过量。教材在这里列了很多解毒剂，大多数不在 BC 范围内，所以你要清楚自己实际能做什么。第三，咬伤和蜇伤。全程留意 PCP 的静脉通路、补液和 D10W 用在哪里。

slides.title: Carbon monoxide: the silent killer
slides.body:
• Binds hemoglobin over 250 times more strongly than oxygen
  • Flu-like: headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion
  • Several sick people in one building → think CO
  • Pulse oximeter can read 99% and be wrong
  • Cherry-red skin is a very late sign
  • CO half-life: about 4 h on room air, about 1.5 h on 100% O₂
slides.say: Carbon monoxide causes more accidental poisoning deaths than any other substance. It comes from burning fuel, like a car in a closed garage or a blocked furnace in winter. It has no colour, smell or taste, and it binds to hemoglobin more than two hundred fifty times more strongly than oxygen. Symptoms look like the flu: headache, nausea, vomiting and confusion. If several people in one building are sick at once, think CO. The trap: your pulse oximeter can't tell carbon monoxide from oxygen, so it may read ninety-nine percent in a badly poisoned patient. Cherry-red skin is a very late sign. Pure oxygen cuts the time CO stays in the blood from about four hours to about one and a half.
slides.sayZh: 一氧化碳造成的意外中毒死亡比任何其他物质都多。它来自燃料燃烧，比如关着门的车库里发动着的车，或者冬天堵塞的暖炉。它无色、无味、无刺激，与血红蛋白的结合力是氧的二百五十倍以上。症状像流感：头痛、恶心、呕吐、意识混乱。同一栋楼里好几个人同时生病，就要想到一氧化碳。陷阱在于：血氧仪分不出一氧化碳和氧，严重中毒的病人也可能显示九十九。樱桃红色皮肤是非常晚期的表现。纯氧能把一氧化碳在血中的清除时间从约四小时缩短到约一个半小时。

slides.title: Cyanide and chlorine
slides.body:
CyanideChlorine
Sourcehouse fires (plastics, wool, foam), industrybleach + acid, pools, tank leaks
Effectcells can't use oxygenforms acid on wet airways
Signsaltered LOC, gasping, BP high then very low, seizuresburning eyes and throat, cough, wheeze, pulmonary edema
Careremove, 100% O₂, ventilateremove, flush eyes and skin, O₂
slides.say: Two more gases to know. Cyanide most often comes from house fires, when plastics, wool carpets and foam burn. It stops the cells from using oxygen, so even with oxygen in the blood, the tissues suffocate. Look for an altered level of consciousness, fast breathing that turns slow and gasping, and a blood pressure that's high at first, then very low. Get the patient out, give one hundred percent oxygen, and ventilate. Chlorine comes from mixing bleach with an acid, from pools, or from tank leaks. It turns into acid on the moist airway, causing burning eyes and throat, coughing, wheezing and, in severe cases, fluid in the lungs. Remove the patient, and flush the eyes and skin with water.
slides.sayZh: 还有两种气体要掌握。氰化物最常来自房屋火灾，塑料、羊毛地毯和泡沫燃烧时产生。它让细胞无法利用氧，所以即使血里有氧，组织也在窒息。表现为意识改变、呼吸先快后变慢喘息、血压先高后极低。把病人移出来，给百分之百氧并通气。氯气来自漂白剂与酸混合、泳池或储罐泄漏。它在湿润的气道上变成酸，引起眼睛和喉咙灼痛、咳嗽、哮鸣，严重时肺里积液。把病人移出来，用清水冲洗眼睛和皮肤。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: gas in the lungs
slides.body:
BC Oxygen Administration + CHF / Pulmonary Edema protocol (its indications include exposure to toxins)

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • CO or smoke: non-rebreather, high flow
  • Sit upright, at rest, keep warm
  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Assist ventilations if LOC altered or SpO₂ < 94%
  • Transport

PCP adds

  • Consider CPAP on scene, if CPAP criteria are met
  • BVM needed? Consider a PEEP valve, start at 5 cmH₂O
  • No CPAP with decreased LOC, vomiting or systolic < 90
slides.say: There's no separate poisoning protocol in BC, so for toxic gases you combine two. The BC oxygen guidelines say carbon monoxide and smoke inhalation call for a non-rebreather mask and high-flow oxygen, so don't turn it down because the saturation looks good. If the gas has injured the lungs, as chlorine can, the CHF or Pulmonary Edema protocol lists exposure to toxins among its indications. Every level sits the patient upright, keeps them at rest and warm, gives oxygen to ninety-four percent or higher, and assists ventilations if the level of consciousness is altered or the saturation is below ninety-four. The PCP adds CPAP on scene if the patient meets the CPAP criteria, or a PEEP valve on the bag, starting at five.
slides.sayZh: BC 没有单独的中毒流程，所以有毒气体要把两个流程结合起来用。BC 的给氧指引规定，一氧化碳中毒和吸入烟雾要用非重复呼吸面罩、高流量氧，所以别因为血氧读数好看就把氧调小。如果气体伤到了肺，比如氯气，CHF 或肺水肿流程的适应证里就包括接触毒物。所有级别都要让病人坐直、休息、保暖，给氧使血氧达到九十四以上，意识改变或血氧低于九十四时辅助通气。PCP 多了：病人符合 CPAP 标准时在现场考虑 CPAP，或者在球囊上加 PEEP 阀，从五开始。

slides.q: On a winter morning, a family of four all have headaches and nausea. The furnace has been acting up. Everyone's SpO₂ reads 98–99%. What is the best plan?
options: Reassure them; a normal SpO₂ rules out carbon monoxide
Move everyone to fresh air and give high-flow oxygen by non-rebreather to all
Give oxygen by nasal cannula only to anyone below 94%
Treat it as a stomach virus and give ondansetron
slides.say: Let's try one. On a winter morning, a family of four all have headaches and nausea. The furnace has been acting up. Everyone's saturation reads ninety-eight to ninety-nine percent. What's the best plan? A, reassure them; a normal saturation rules out carbon monoxide. B, move everyone to fresh air and give high-flow oxygen by non-rebreather to all. C, give oxygen by nasal cannula only to anyone below ninety-four percent. D, treat it as a stomach virus and give ondansetron. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来做一题。冬天早上，一家四口都头痛、恶心，家里的暖炉最近不太正常。每个人的血氧都是九十八到九十九。最好的方案是什么？A 安慰他们，血氧正常就排除了一氧化碳；B 让所有人到新鲜空气处，全部用非重复呼吸面罩给高流量氧；C 只给血氧低于九十四的人用鼻导管吸氧；D 当作胃肠炎处理，给昂丹司琼。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Several people sick in the same house, with a faulty furnace in winter, is carbon monoxide until proven otherwise. A standard pulse oximeter can't tell CO from oxygen, so ninety-eight or ninety-nine percent means nothing here. BC calls for a non-rebreather and high-flow oxygen for CO poisoning, so A and C are wrong. D treats a symptom and leaves the family breathing the gas; an antiemetic won't fix the real problem.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。冬天、暖炉有问题、同一屋子好几个人生病，在排除之前就是一氧化碳中毒。普通血氧仪分不出一氧化碳和氧，所以九十八、九十九在这里没有意义。BC 规定一氧化碳中毒用非重复呼吸面罩、高流量氧，所以 A 和 C 都错。D 只治症状，还让一家人继续吸着气体；止吐药解决不了真正的问题。

slides.title: Organophosphates: the wet patient
slides.body:
• Farm and garden pesticides; nerve agents are the same family
  • Acetylcholine isn't cleared → DUMBELS + muscle weakness
  • Skin, lungs or gut: the same picture
  • Decontaminate first: strip, bag clothing, soap and water
  • Then airway, lots of suction, high-flow O₂, ventilate
  • Antidotes atropine and pralidoxime: not in BC scope
slides.say: Organophosphates and carbamates are pesticides, and nerve agents belong to the same family. They block the enzyme that clears acetylcholine, so the nerves keep firing. The result is the wet, cholinergic patient: DUMBELS, plus muscle weakness, confusion and seizures. Skin contact, breathing it in or swallowing it all give the same picture. Decontamination comes first: remove all clothing, bag it as hazardous waste, and wash the patient with soap and water, often with a hazmat team, before the patient enters your ambulance. Wear protection, because even vomit can contaminate you. Then manage the airway, suction a lot, give high-flow oxygen and ventilate. The antidotes, atropine and pralidoxime, are not in BC EMR or PCP scope.
slides.sayZh: 有机磷和氨基甲酸酯是农药，神经毒剂也属于同一类。它们阻断清除乙酰胆碱的酶，让神经不停放电。结果就是「湿」的胆碱能病人：DUMBELS，加上肌无力、意识混乱和抽搐。皮肤接触、吸入或吞下，表现都一样。洗消第一：脱掉所有衣物，按危险废物装袋，用肥皂和水清洗病人，通常和危险品小组一起，在病人上救护车之前完成。要穿防护，因为连呕吐物都可能污染你。然后管理气道、大量吸引、给高流量氧并通气。解毒剂阿托品和解磷定都不在 BC EMR 和 PCP 范围内。

slides.title: Pain pills: acetaminophen and ASA
slides.body:
AcetaminophenASA (salicylate)
Toxic doseover 150–200 mg/kg150–300 mg/kg moderate; 300 mg/kg severe
Early signsmay be none; nausea, vomitingvomiting, ringing ears, fast deep breathing
Dangerliver failure days lateracid–base chaos; brain and lung swelling
Antidotehospital only; best within 8–10 hnone; supportive care

Hidden in many cold and pain products. Time of ingestion matters.
slides.say: Over-the-counter pain pills cause many serious overdoses, because people think they're harmless. Acetaminophen becomes toxic above about one hundred fifty to two hundred milligrams per kilogram taken at once, and it hides in many cold and pain products. The scary part: a deadly dose can cause no symptoms at first, then liver failure days later. The hospital antidote works best within eight to ten hours, so your most useful finding is the time of ingestion. ASA, a salicylate, causes vomiting, ringing in the ears and fast, deep breathing, and severe cases cause brain and lung swelling. There's no antidote, only supportive care. In a confused older patient, chronic ASA poisoning is easy to miss.
slides.sayZh: 非处方止痛药引起很多严重过量，因为大家以为它们无害。对乙酰氨基酚一次服用超过每公斤约一百五十到两百毫克就会中毒，而且它藏在很多感冒药和止痛药里。可怕之处在于：致死量一开始可以完全没有症状，几天后才肝衰竭。医院的解毒剂在八到十小时内效果最好，所以你最有用的信息是服药时间。阿司匹林（ASA，水杨酸类）会引起呕吐、耳鸣和深快呼吸，重者脑水肿、肺水肿；没有解毒剂，只能支持治疗。在意识混乱的老人身上，慢性阿司匹林中毒很容易漏诊。

slides.title: Caustics, hydrocarbons, toxic alcohols
slides.body:
• Caustics: acid pH < 2, alkali pH > 12; alkali burns deeper
  • Just swallowed, alert: one glass of water or milk; never neutralize
  • Trouble talking or breathing → airway swelling: go now
  • Hydrocarbons: thin liquids get aspirated; coughing = aspiration
  • Toxic alcohols: look drunk, no alcohol smell, delayed signs
  • Methanol: 30 mL can kill or blind; ethylene glycol: kidney failure
slides.say: Household chemicals cause many calls, especially in children. Caustics are strong acids or alkalis, like drain cleaner. Alkalis burn deeper because the pain starts later. If the patient is alert and just swallowed it, give one glass of water or milk to dilute it, but never try to neutralize it; that creates heat and a second burn. Trouble talking or breathing means the throat is swelling, so move fast. Hydrocarbons, like gasoline or lamp oil, are thin liquids that slip into the lungs, so coughing after a swallow means aspiration. Toxic alcohols, methanol and antifreeze, make a patient look drunk with no alcohol smell, and the worst signs come hours later. As little as thirty millilitres of methanol can kill or blind.
slides.sayZh: 家用化学品引起很多呼叫，尤其是儿童。腐蚀剂是强酸或强碱，比如下水道疏通剂。碱烧得更深，因为疼痛来得晚。如果病人清醒、刚刚吞下，给一杯水或牛奶稀释，但绝不要中和，中和会产热、造成第二次烧伤。说话或呼吸困难说明喉咙在肿，要立刻走。烃类，比如汽油或灯油，是稀薄的液体，很容易进入肺里，所以吞下后咳嗽就意味着误吸。有毒醇类，甲醇和防冻液，让病人看起来像醉了却没有酒味，最严重的表现几小时后才出现。少到三十毫升甲醇就可能致死或致盲。

slides.title: Prescription drug overdoses
slides.body:
DrugWatch for
Heart pills (beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers, digoxin)"slow and low": bradycardia + hypotension
Tricyclic antidepressantsdry, hot, fast pulse → wide QRS, seizure, sudden arrest
SSRIs + other serotonin drugsserotonin syndrome: fever, sweating, tremor, confusion
Lithiumvomiting, tremor → confusion, seizures
Sulfonylurea diabetes pillslong, repeated hypoglycemia
slides.say: Prescription drugs are a big part of overdose calls. Heart medicines like beta-blockers, calcium channel blockers and digoxin cause the slow and low pattern: a slow heart rate and low blood pressure. Tricyclic antidepressants are the most treacherous. At first they look anticholinergic: dry, hot, a fast pulse. But they can suddenly widen the QRS complex, cause seizures or stop the heart; the patient can be drowsy one minute and arresting the next. SSRIs combined with other serotonin drugs can cause serotonin syndrome: fever, sweating, tremor and confusion. Lithium causes vomiting and tremor, then confusion and seizures. And sulfonylureas, a type of diabetes pill, cause long-lasting low blood sugar; one tablet can kill a toddler.
slides.sayZh: 处方药在过量呼叫中占很大比例。β 受体阻滞剂、钙通道阻滞剂和地高辛等心脏药引起「慢而低」：心率慢、血压低。三环类抗抑郁药最阴险：一开始像抗胆碱能中毒，干、热、心率快，但可以突然 QRS 增宽、抽搐或心脏骤停；病人前一分钟还只是嗜睡，下一分钟就骤停。SSRI 与其他 5-羟色胺类药物合用会引起 5-羟色胺综合征：发热、出汗、震颤和意识混乱。锂中毒先呕吐、手抖，然后意识混乱和抽搐。磺脲类降糖药会引起持续很久的低血糖，一片就可能要了幼儿的命。

slides.q: A 72-year-old took extra doses of her sulfonylurea diabetes pill today. She is drowsy and cannot protect her airway. BGL is 2.4 mmol/L. As the PCP, what is the best plan?
options: Oral glucose gel, then leave her at home once she wakes up
IV, D10W 10–25 g, transport, and recheck her BGL often
Glucagon IM first, and an IV only if that fails
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. A seventy-two-year-old took extra doses of her sulfonylurea diabetes pill today. She's drowsy and can't protect her airway. Her glucose is two point four. As the PCP, what's the best plan? A, oral glucose gel, then leave her at home once she wakes up. B, an IV, D10W ten to twenty-five grams, transport, and recheck her glucose often. C, activated charcoal first, then D10W. D, glucagon IM first, and an IV only if that fails. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。一位七十二岁女性今天多吃了几次磺脲类降糖药。她嗜睡，不能保护自己的气道，血糖二点四。作为 PCP，最好的方案是什么？A 口服葡萄糖凝胶，等她醒了就让她留在家里；B 开静脉，给 D10W 十到二十五克，转运，并经常复测血糖；C 先给活性炭，再给 D10W；D 先肌注胰高血糖素，失败了才开静脉。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. For confirmed low sugar, the PCP starts an IV, gives D10W ten to twenty-five grams, and transports. Sulfonylureas act for a long time, so her sugar can drop again; recheck it often en route. A is wrong twice: she can't protect her airway, and she can't safely stay home. C is wrong because activated charcoal is not in BC EMR or PCP scope. D reverses the PCP order; glucagon is for when you can't get IV access.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。确认低血糖时，PCP 开静脉、给 D10W 十到二十五克，然后转运。磺脲类作用时间长，她的血糖可能再次下降，途中要经常复测。A 错两处：她不能保护气道，也不能安全地留在家里。C 错在活性炭不在 BC EMR 和 PCP 范围内。D 把 PCP 的顺序弄反了，胰高血糖素是开不了静脉时才用的。

slides.title: Bites and stings
slides.body:
• Bees, wasps, ants: most deaths are from anaphylaxis
  • Scrape the stinger off; don't squeeze it with tweezers
  • Canada: 3 native venomous snakes, all pit vipers
  • 1 bite in 4 is "dry"; you can't tell on scene
  • Calm, supine, still; limb neutral; no tight bands, no ice
  • Call the Poison Centre; transport (antivenom in hospital)
slides.say: Bees, wasps and ants kill more people each year than any other venomous animals, including snakes, almost always through anaphylaxis, so the BC Anaphylaxis protocol is the real treatment: epinephrine for every licence level, and the PCP adds fluids, salbutamol and diphenhydramine. To remove a bee stinger, scrape it off; squeezing it with tweezers pushes in more venom. Canada has three native venomous snakes, all pit vipers, including the Northern Pacific rattlesnake in B.C. About one bite in four is dry, with no venom, but you can't tell on scene. Keep the patient calm, lying down and still, with the limb in a neutral position. No tight bands, and no ice. Call the Poison Centre and transport.
slides.sayZh: 蜜蜂、黄蜂和蚂蚁每年致死的人数比其他任何有毒动物都多，包括蛇，而且几乎都是死于过敏性休克，所以真正的治疗是 BC 过敏性休克流程：所有级别都给肾上腺素，PCP 再加补液、沙丁胺醇和苯海拉明。取蜜蜂的刺要刮掉，用镊子夹会把更多毒液挤进去。加拿大有三种原生毒蛇，都是蝮蛇，包括 BC 的北太平洋响尾蛇。大约四分之一的咬伤是「干咬」，没有注入毒液，但现场分辨不出来。让病人保持平静、平躺不动，患肢放在中立位。不要扎紧束带，不要冰敷。联系中毒中心并转运。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• CO: the pulse oximeter lies; treat the patient, not the number
  • Delayed killers (acetaminophen, toxic alcohols): looks well ≠ is well
  • Tricyclics: drowsy → seizure or arrest in a moment
  • Sulfonylurea lows come back: recheck BGL often
  • Decontaminate before the IV and before loading
  • CPAP: not with vomiting, decreased LOC or systolic < 90
slides.say: Here are the PCP watch-outs for this group of poisons. With carbon monoxide, the pulse oximeter lies, so treat the patient, not the number. Some poisons are delayed killers: acetaminophen and the toxic alcohols can look harmless for hours, so a patient who looks well may not be well, and needs transport. A tricyclic overdose can go from drowsy to seizing or arresting in a moment; keep suction and the bag-valve mask ready. Low sugar from sulfonylureas comes back after D10W, so recheck the glucose often. With pesticides, decontaminate before you start an IV or load the patient. And CPAP is not for a patient who is vomiting, has a decreased level of consciousness, or has a systolic under ninety.
slides.sayZh: 这一类毒物的 PCP 注意事项：一氧化碳中毒时血氧仪会骗人，要治病人，不是治读数。有些毒物是迟发杀手：对乙酰氨基酚和有毒醇类可能几个小时看起来都没事，所以看起来好不等于真的好，需要转运。三环类过量可以一瞬间从嗜睡变成抽搐或骤停，吸引器和球囊面罩要随时备好。磺脲类引起的低血糖在给完 D10W 后还会再来，要经常复测血糖。农药中毒要先洗消，再开静脉或上车。CPAP 不能用于正在呕吐、意识水平下降或收缩压低于九十的病人。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Not in BC EMR/PCP scope: atropine, pralidoxime, activated charcoal, benzodiazepines, IO
  • Not BC drugs: hydroxocobalamin, nitrites, bicarbonate, calcium, NAC, fomepizole
  • Book gives D50W for low sugar → BC: D10W 10–25 g
  • CO or smoke: non-rebreather, high-flow O₂
  • Epinephrine in BC: IM only
slides.say: Now the BC exam points. The book offers many antidotes in this section, and you need to know they're not yours. Atropine, pralidoxime, activated charcoal, benzodiazepines and intraosseous access are not in BC EMR or PCP scope. Hydroxocobalamin, the nitrites, sodium bicarbonate, calcium gluconate, N-acetylcysteine and fomepizole are not among the eighteen BC exam drugs. Where the book gives D50W for low sugar in a tricyclic overdose, BC's only IV dextrose is D10W, ten to twenty-five grams. For carbon monoxide or smoke, BC calls for a non-rebreather and high-flow oxygen. And epinephrine for a sting with anaphylaxis is IM only in BC.
slides.sayZh: 现在看 BC 考点。书里这一部分提供了很多解毒剂，你要知道它们都不是你的。阿托品、解磷定、活性炭、苯二氮卓类和骨髓腔通路都不在 BC EMR 和 PCP 范围内。羟钴胺、亚硝酸盐类、碳酸氢钠、葡萄糖酸钙、N-乙酰半胱氨酸和甲吡唑都不在 BC 十八种考试药物里。书里对三环类过量的低血糖给 D50W，而 BC 唯一的静脉葡萄糖是 D10W，十到二十五克。一氧化碳中毒或吸入烟雾，BC 要求用非重复呼吸面罩、高流量氧。蜇伤引起的过敏性休克，BC 的肾上腺素只能肌注。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Gases: get out, non-rebreather for CO and smoke; PCP adds CPAP / PEEP when criteria fit
  2. Antidotes are mostly outside BC scope: you give airway, O₂, decon, fluids, D10W
  3. Delayed and long-acting poisons: transport and reassess, even if the patient looks well

Next: Chapter 37, Hematologic Emergencies
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: with toxic gases, get the patient out and give high-flow oxygen by non-rebreather for carbon monoxide and smoke, whatever the saturation says; if the lungs are injured, the PCP can add CPAP or PEEP when the criteria fit. Two: most of the book's antidotes are outside BC scope. Your tools are the airway, oxygen, decontamination, fluids, and D10W for confirmed low sugar. Three: some poisons are delayed or long-acting, like acetaminophen, toxic alcohols and sulfonylureas, so transport and keep reassessing even when the patient looks well. Next time: Chapter 37, hematologic emergencies. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 记住三件事。一，有毒气体：把病人移出来，一氧化碳和烟雾不管血氧读数是多少都用非重复呼吸面罩给高流量氧；如果肺受了伤，符合标准时 PCP 可以加 CPAP 或 PEEP。二，书里的大多数解毒剂不在 BC 范围内，你的工具是气道、氧气、洗消、补液，以及对确认低血糖给 D10W。三，有些毒物是迟发或长效的，比如对乙酰氨基酚、有毒醇类和磺脲类，所以即使病人看起来没事，也要转运并持续复评。下节课：第三十七章，血液系统急症。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
